Subject: Entitlements gatecheck / SSO & SCIM kickoff

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. The executive team at FinCrest signed off on moving to Redwood for inference serving, and security wants to run a quick "entitlements gatecheck" before we schedule the full implementation. High level asks from our side:

- Confirm SAML attributes you require (NameID format, groups, email) and whether we need any custom claims.
- SCIM user/role mapping template — we have complex role names in our HRIS and want to ensure a deterministic mapping.
- IP allowlist range for the private connector and the service account pattern for automation (what scopes will the service account need?).
- Any org-level policies that will block provisioning (e.g., restricted domains, MFA enforcement).

I've attached our SAML metadata dump (FinCrest_SAML_Metadata.xml) and put security_ops on cc. Can someone from your implementation team share a short pre-call checklist and the mapping template so we can validate internally ahead of the kickoff?

We'd like to hold the technical pre-call tomorrow afternoon if possible.

Best,
Lucia
Lucia Ramos
Director, IT Security
FinCrest Capital

Hi Lucia — great news on the exec sign-off, congrats.

We can run the gatecheck and provide a concise pre-call artifact set. I've looped in Marissa (implementation lead) and Karthik (access controls). Proposed next steps:

1) Pre-call packet (we'll send as Drive links): required SAML attributes, SCIM mapping CSV, service-account naming & scopes, recommended IP allowlist CIDR blocks, and a short org-policy checklist.
2) 30-minute technical pre-call to confirm mappings and confirm which HRIS fields you will push (we'll ask for a staging tenant for SCIM testing).
3) Implementation runbook delivery and canary plan after gatecheck.

We can deliver the pre-call packet within 2 hours and meet at 14:30 PT tomorrow — does that work for your team?

Jonas

Hi Lucia — thanks for the metadata. I'm attaching two quick artifacts you can validate immediately:

- redwood-scim-mapping.csv (stub) — column headers include scimPath, sourceField, transform, default, roleTarget. We'll map your HRIS roles to Redwood roles; if there are nested role sets we recommend a dedicated sync user.
- ip-allowlist-template.csv (stub) — includes suggested CIDRs for private connector and a separate column for egress ranges for long-running batch jobs.

Notes / clarifications from engineering:
- SAML: We accept persistent NameID or email; we require groups in claims as a semicolon-separated attribute named "roles" or as standard "groups" depending on your IdP. If you plan to use encrypted assertions let us know — it requires additional config.
- SCIM: We support /Users and /Groups v2 endpoints. We do not yet support custom complex attributes — we'll propose a transform step in the mapping CSV.
- Service accounts: recommended pattern: svc-redwood-<env>-<team>. They need two scopes: inference.read (for read-only token exchange during onboarding) and provisioning.write (for SCIM pushes). We'll provide least-privilege scopes for production after cutover.
- Org policies: if your org blocks app provisioning from external domains we will need an allowlist for redwoodinference.com and a short-term exception for the staging tenant.

Attachments: redwood-scim-mapping.csv, ip-allowlist-template.csv.

We will also include a short checklist in the pre-call packet with gating criteria (IdP metadata validated, SCIM test push successful, IPs whitelisted, service account created).

--
Marissa Cole
Implementation Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
